full_judgment:
M.H. Rahman, J : Respondents filed a suit, S.C.C. Suit No. 1 of 1982 in the Court of Munsif, Second Court, Serajganj, for the eviction of the defendants-appellants from the suit premises. That suit was decreed ex-parte on 9th March, 1983. On 11th August, 1983, the appellants filed Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 1983 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Section 17 of the Small Cause Courts Act, 1887, for setting aside the ex-parte decree. On that date the appellants application praying for exemption from depositing the security money till the hearing of the miscellaneous case was also allowed. The case was fixed for peremptory hearing on 30th July, 1984, but the appellants took time on that date and on several subsequent dates. On 31st December, 1985, the appellants filed a security bond with an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act read with Section 151 of the Code for acceptance of the bond on condonation of delay. The S.S.C. Judge refused to condone the delay, rejected the security bond and dismissed the Miscellaneous case as not maintainable. In revision the High Court Division upheld the order of the learned S.C.C. Judge. 

 4. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division observed that at the time of the presentation of the application under Section 17 of the S.C.C. Act, the appellants did not furnish the security deposit nor did make any application seeking the necessary direction of the Court; that after a lapse of about 2 years and 8 months they made a prayer for time to furnish the requisite security; that the S.C.C. Judge refused the prayer and set down the case for hearing on 26th December, 1985, but even on that day the appellants made no attempt to furnish the security and that when the matter came up again for hearing on 31st December, 1985, they filed a security bond with a prayer for its acceptance after condonation of delay. 

 5. It is true that on 11th August, 1983, the petitioner's prayer for exemption was allowed till the hearing of the Miscellaneous case. The Miscellaneous case came up for the premptory hearing on 30th July, 1984, and thereafter several dates were fixed for peremptory hearing, but the appellants did not comply with the requirements under proviso to Section 17(1) on or before the date when the matter was fixed for pre-emptory hearing. 

 6. The Court can extend time for compliance with the proviso to Section 17(1), but it cannot give an extension of time till the hearing of the matter, as wrongly granted in this case, as that would frustrate the very purpose of that proviso. This is not a case where the litigant suffers from the wrong order of the Court. This is case where a defaulter wants to take advantage of an order wrongly passed by the Court. We find it difficult to understand why there was so much delay in filing a security bond, rather a simple matter. The delay was due to negligence and the learned S.C.C. Judge rightly refused to condone the same.
